questions.stem: At dynamic equilibrium in a closed system,

options.text: both the forward and backward reactions have stopped
the rates of the forward and backward reactions are equal
the concentrations of reactants and products are always equal
all the reactants have been used up

questions.explanation: Equilibrium is dynamic, not static. Both reactions carry on at the molecular level, but because they proceed at identical rates there is no net change in any concentration, so the mixture appears unchanging from outside.

distractorRationale.a: The reactions continue; only the net change is zero
distractorRationale.c: Concentrations become constant, but they are hardly ever equal to one another
distractorRationale.d: Some reactant always remains, which is precisely why the reaction is incomplete

questions.stem: For the equilibrium 2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g), increasing the total pressure will

options.text: shift the equilibrium to the left
shift the equilibrium to the right
have no effect on the position of equilibrium
stop the reaction entirely

questions.explanation: There are 3 moles of gas on the left and 2 on the right. By Le Chatelier's principle the system opposes the increase in pressure by moving to the side with fewer gas molecules, so the equilibrium shifts right and more sulphur(VI) oxide is formed.

distractorRationale.a: Shifting left would increase the number of gas molecules and raise the pressure further
distractorRationale.c: Pressure has no effect only when the moles of gas are equal on both sides, which is not the case here
distractorRationale.d: Changing pressure alters the position of equilibrium; it never halts the reaction

questions.stem: Adding a catalyst to a system at equilibrium

options.text: shifts the equilibrium to the right
shifts the equilibrium to the left
does not change the position of equilibrium but is reached sooner
increases the value of the equilibrium constant

questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the forward and backward reactions by the same amount, so both rates increase by the same factor. Equilibrium is therefore reached more quickly, but the final composition and the value of Kc are unchanged.

distractorRationale.a: A shift would require the two rates to be affected unequally, which a catalyst does not do
distractorRationale.b: The same reasoning rules out a leftward shift
distractorRationale.d: Kc depends only on temperature, not on the presence of a catalyst

questions.stem: For the exothermic equilibrium N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g), the yield of ammonia is increased by

options.text: raising the temperature and lowering the pressure
lowering the temperature and raising the pressure
raising both the temperature and the pressure
adding more catalyst

questions.explanation: Since the forward reaction is exothermic, cooling the system drives it forward to replace the heat removed. There are 4 moles of gas on the left and 2 on the right, so raising the pressure also drives it forward. In practice a compromise temperature of about 450 degrees Celsius is used because a low temperature makes the reaction far too slow.

distractorRationale.a: Both changes push the equilibrium backwards and reduce the yield
distractorRationale.c: Higher pressure helps but higher temperature works against the exothermic forward reaction
distractorRationale.d: A catalyst speeds up the approach to equilibrium without altering the yield

questions.stem: For the equilibrium H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g), the correct expression for the equilibrium constant Kc is
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant places the products in the numerator and the reactants in the denominator, with each concentration raised to the power of its coefficient in the balanced equation. Hydrogen iodide has a coefficient of 2, so its concentration is squared.

distractorRationale.a: Products and reactants have been swapped; this is the constant for the reverse reaction
distractorRationale.c: The coefficient must appear as a power, not as a multiplier
distractorRationale.d: Concentrations of reactants are multiplied together, never added

questions.stem: A dynamic equilibrium can be established in an open beaker in which one of the products is a gas that escapes.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Equilibrium requires a closed system. If a gaseous product escapes, the backward reaction can never build up to match the forward rate, so the system is continually pulled to the right and the reaction goes to completion instead of reaching equilibrium.
